content:
When Israel walked through the wilderness, Yahweh fed them with a food no human being had ever seen before. There were no fields to harvest, no grain to grind, and no shops from which such a great multitude could buy food.

Yet every day Yahweh placed food around their camp. And in that daily bread, He hid many beautiful pictures of His own Word. Today we begin to gather some of the precious lessons that the manna holds for us as the New Creation.

Exodus 16:14-15 says, "When the dew evaporated, a flaky substance as fine as frost blanketed the ground. The Israelites were puzzled when they saw it. 'What is it?' they asked each other. They had no idea what it was". When the people first saw this strange food, they asked one another, "What is it?" The Hebrew words sound like man hu, and from that very question came the name manna. This gives us our first lesson. When we come to the Word of Yahweh, we must come with a humble and wondering heart, asking, "What is this? What is Yahweh teaching me? What is hidden here in this passage?" We should never approach the Scriptures as though we already know everything. The bread of heaven is not received by the proud heart. It is gathered by those who are willing to bend low, search carefully, and receive instruction. The Israelites could not stand at a distance and merely look at the manna. They had to bend down and gather it. In the same way, spiritual truth requires humility. We must lower our own opinions, our traditions, and our human wisdom before we can receive what Yahweh has placed in His Word.

Numbers 11:9 says, "The manna came down on the camp with the dew during the night". The dew came during the quiet, dark hours of the night, and when the morning came and the dew lifted, the fine manna became visible upon the ground. We may compare the dew to the words of Yahweh. Dew comes quietly and gently. It does not fall with the force of a storm. Moses said, "Let my teaching fall on you like rain; let my speech settle like dew" (Deuteronomy 32:2,). But notice that the manna was connected with the dew. Underneath the outward words of Scripture lies the deeper truth and purpose of Yahweh. Many people read the words but never search for the hidden plan contained within them. They see the dew, but they do not gather the manna. They read the verse, but they do not search for its meaning. They hear the words, but they never allow the truth to enter their hearts. Proverbs 25:2 says, "It is God's privilege to conceal things and the king's privilege to discover them". Yahweh has placed many treasures within His Word. They are not hidden so that they can never be found. They are hidden so that faithful seekers may search, discover, and truly value them. We must never be satisfied with reading only the surface of a passage. We must pray, compare Scripture with Scripture, and ask Yahweh to help us understand the truth that lies within His words.

The manna came in the darkness, but it became visible only when the morning arrived and the dew lifted. In the same way, the Word of Yahweh may remain dark to us until light is given. And Christ is the light through whom the Scriptures are opened. He said, "I am the light of the world. If you follow me, you won't have to walk in darkness, because you will have the light that leads to life" (John 8:12). The scribes and Pharisees possessed the scrolls of Scripture. They read the words and taught them to others. Yet many of them did not recognise the Messiah when he stood before them. They had the written words, but they did not allow the light of Christ to reveal their true meaning. After the resurrection, two disciples travelled toward Emmaus, and Christ joined them and explained the Scriptures concerning himself. Later they said, "Didn't our hearts burn within us as he talked with us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?" (Luke 24:32). The verses had been there all along, but when Christ opened them, the hidden meaning became clear. The manna had been present, but now the light revealed it. So we too should ask Yahweh to give us the light of Christ whenever we read the Bible. Without that light, we may see only words. With that light, we begin to see the purpose, the harmony, and the beauty of Yahweh's plan.

The manna was also very small. Exodus 16:14 calls it "a flaky substance as fine as frost," and Exodus 16:31 says, "The manna looked like small coriander seeds". It looked small and simple, yet this small food sustained an entire nation throughout the wilderness. This reminds us of the Word of Yahweh, for Christ said, "The seed is God's word" (Luke 8:11). A seed is small when it rests in the hand, but inside it is the life of a future plant. A great tree may begin with a seed that appears almost insignificant. In the same way, one small verse can contain great spiritual life. A single promise can strengthen a person through many years of trial. One command can change the direction of a whole life. One truth, planted deeply in the heart, can grow into faith, obedience, patience, and hope. We must never despise the small things of Yahweh. A short verse may look simple. A familiar passage may appear ordinary. A quiet Morning Light study may seem small. Yet when the seed of the Word enters a faithful heart, it can produce a great harvest. The wisdom of the world may appear large and impressive, but the smallest seed of Yahweh's truth contains more life than all human wisdom put together.

The manna was also described as white or pale in colour, clean and pure in its appearance. This reminds us that the words of Yahweh are pure. Psalm 12:6 says, "The LORD's promises are pure, like silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times over". The Word of Yahweh does not contain confusion, or deception found in human thinking. It is pure and trustworthy. The manna lay upon the dusty wilderness ground, yet it came from heaven. In the same way, the Word of Yahweh has been given to people living in a sinful world, but its source is far above. It must therefore be handled with reverence. We should never mix the pure Word with human traditions, personal imaginations, or teachings that stand against Scripture.

So far, we have seen the manna as something to wonder at, something hidden beneath the dew, something revealed only by the light of Christ, small like a seed yet full of life, and pure and white like the very promises of Yahweh.

But there is much more still hidden in this bread from heaven. We have not yet tasted its sweetness, nor understood the richness of the oil in it, nor learned why it had to be gathered fresh with our own hands every single morning.Each of these carries a lesson we must not miss. That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We come to Your Word as Israel came to the manna, asking humbly, 'What is it?'

Give us the light of Christ to open the Scriptures and reveal what is hidden within them. Teach us to bend low, to search carefully, and never to despise the smallest seed of Your truth. Keep us from the pride that reads only the surface and misses the treasure beneath.

Make us humble seekers who gather the pure bread You have given from above.

"Open my eyes to see the wonderful truths in your instructions." - Psalm 119:18

In the name of Christ, the true bread from heaven, we pray. Amen.
